title: Second-Order Linear Equations and Superposition
short: Combinations of solutions of a homogeneous linear equation are solutions.

blocks.html: A second-order linear equation has the form $a(t)y'' + b(t)y' + c(t)y$ $= g(t)$. It is homogeneous when $g = 0$. Second-order equations describe springs, pendulums, circuits and beams, and their solutions have a structure you met in Linear Independence: they form a vector space.

Superposition: if $y_1$ and $y_2$ solve a linear homogeneous equation, so does $c_1y_1 + c_2y_2$ for any constants. If $y_1$ and $y_2$ are independent, every solution has this form (the general solution). For the nonhomogeneous equation, every solution is $$y = y_p + c_1y_1 + c_2y_2,$$ where $y_p$ is any one particular solution.

Write $L[y] = a y'' + b y' + c y$. Derivatives respect sums and constant multiples, so $L[c_1y_1 + c_2y_2]$ $= c_1L[y_1] + c_2L[y_2] = 0 + 0$. For the nonhomogeneous equation, if $y$ and $y_p$ both solve $L[y] = g$, then $L[y - y_p] = g - g = 0$: their difference is a homogeneous solution. Finally, two initial conditions $y(t_0), y'(t_0)$ pick out exactly one solution, and two independent solutions are enough to match any pair of initial values. So the solution set is two-dimensional, like the null space of a matrix.

blocks.title: Fit two constants
blocks.q: $y_1 = e^{2t}$ and $y_2 = e^{-t}$ solve $y'' - y' - 2y = 0$. Find the solution with $y(0) = 1$, $y'(0) = 5$.
steps: By superposition, $y = c_1e^{2t} + c_2e^{-t}$, with $y' = 2c_1e^{2t} - c_2e^{-t}$.

blocks.title: A nonhomogeneous equation
blocks.q: Check that $y_p = -2$ solves $y'' - y' - 2y = 4$, then solve with $y(0) = 0$, $y'(0) = 1$.

blocks.html: Superposition is only for homogeneous linear equations. Adding two solutions of $L[y] = g$ gives $L[y_1 + y_2] = 2g$, not $g$; and for a nonlinear equation such as $y'' = -y^{2}$, sums of solutions are not solutions at all. Products like $y_1y_2$ are never covered.

blocks.name: graph
blocks.cap: Every setting of the sliders gives a solution $y = ae^{-t} + be^{-2t}$ of $y'' + 3y' + 2y = 0$. Two numbers are enough to reach any starting height and slope at $t = 0$.
